newsitem.title: USA: Pieces of shuttle Challenger wash ashore in Miami.
newsitem.headline: Pieces of shuttle Challenger wash ashore in Miami.

text.p: Two large pieces of the space shuttle Challenger were found on a Florida beach on Tuesday, more than a decade after the craft exploded shortly after takeoff, a NASA spokeswoman said.
NASA officials said they knew the wreckage was from Challenger because it bore some of the shuttle's protective tiles.

The wreckage, one piece measuring 15 feet by six feet (4.5-by-two-meters) and another about five feet by one foot (1.5-by-.3-meters), was found along a stretch of Cocoa Beach near oceanfront condominiums, bars and restaurants.
Challenger exploded 73 second after liftoff on Jan. 28, 1986, killing all seven crew members including schoolteacher Christa McAuliffe.
About half of the shuttle's wreckage was never found and pieces have occasionally washed ashore in the ensuing ten years, though NASA said Tuesday's finds were unusually large.
The wreckage was being loaded onto trucks to be taken back to the Kennedy Space Centre for examination.
